title: From mechanism to application: Harnessing oxidative stress signaling for innovative food design.
authors: Xu, Caihong; Chen, Xi; Yang, Qingyu
one_liner_zh: 该文综述氧化应激信号通路在功能性食品设计中的应用，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: As a central pathological process in aging and chronic diseases, oxidative stress (OS) stems from redox imbalance and propagates cellular damage through tightly linked signaling networks. Traditional functional food approaches, which focus on single-pathway interventions, fail to counter the complex crosstalk and compensatory adaptations seen in OS-related pathologies. In this article, we provide a systematic analysis of six key signaling pathways, namely Nrf2/ARE, FOXO, NF-kappaB, p53, SIRT1, and AMPK, and delineate their hierarchical structure and functional interactions in modulating antioxidant defense, metabolic reprogramming, and cell fate. We advocate for a multi-pathway synergistic strategy, rooted in rational systemic nutrition, to achieve coordinated control over redox balance, inflammatory responses, and metabolic homeostasis, thereby delivering efficacy beyond conventional single-target paradigms. To tackle persistent challenges such as nonlinear dose responses and interspecies metabolic variation, we propose a data-driven design framework that combines computational prediction, physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling, and spatiotemporally precise nutrient delivery systems. Integrated with deep learning and human-relevant validation platforms, for instance organ-on-a-chip technology and multi-omics profiling, this framework accelerates the creation of personalized functional foods suited to individual physiological requirements. Our findings establish a theoretical basis for network-based nutritional design, driving the evolution of functional foods from empirical recipes to precision tools for systemic health restoration.
abstract_zh: 作为衰老和慢性疾病中的核心病理过程，氧化应激（oxidative stress, OS）源于氧化还原失衡，并通过紧密关联的信号网络传播细胞损伤。传统的功能性食品方法侧重于单通路干预，无法应对OS相关病理中复杂的交叉对话和代偿性适应。在本文中，我们对六条关键信号通路，即Nrf2/ARE、FOXO、NF-kappaB、p53、SIRT1和AMPK，进行了系统分析，并描绘了它们在调节抗氧化防御、代谢重编程和细胞命运中的层级结构及功能相互作用。我们倡导一种基于理性系统营养学的多通路协同策略，以实现对氧化还原平衡、炎症反应和代谢稳态的协调控制，从而提供超越传统单靶点范式的疗效。为应对非线性剂量反应和跨物种代谢变异等持续挑战，我们提出了一种数据驱动的设计框架，该框架结合了计算预测、生理药代动力学建模和时空精准营养递送系统。结合深度学习及人类相关验证平台，例如器官芯片技术和多组学分析，该框架加速了适合个体生理需求的个性化功能性食品的开发。我们的发现为基于网络的营养设计奠定了理论基础，推动功能性食品从经验配方演变为系统性健康恢复的精准工具。
